description: The bar chart illustrates the % point difference in morphosyntactic probing performance between two multilingual BERT models — mBERT (light blue) and XLM-R (dark blue) — across four different classifier configurations, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The horizontal axis lists the classifier configurations: “hidden:[50], linear,” “hidden:[], linear,” “hidden:[100], ReLU,” and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” while the vertical axis represents the % point difference, ranging from –0.2 to +0.2, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. For “hidden:[50], linear,” mBERT shows a negative difference of approximately –0.18, while XLM-R is slightly negative at around –0.05. In “hidden:[], linear,” both models show positive differences, with mBERT at ~+0.09 and XLM-R at ~+0.20. For “hidden:[100], ReLU,” mBERT is negative at ~–0.12 and XLM-R is slightly positive at ~+0.03. Finally, in “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” mBERT is at ~–0.18 and XLM-R at ~–0.12. The bars are grouped by configuration, with mBERT always on the left and XLM-R on the right within each group, and no bars are shaded or emphasized beyond their color coding. The chart suggests that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT in linear classifiers, especially with no hidden layers, while performance diverges in ReLU-based configurations.
